customer_question: We are registering a module using a Qualcomm chipset that supports Class 1 (high power, long range) Bluetooth. When we set RF ICS item 1/1 to 'Supported' (Class 1), we get an 'Invalid' Consistency Check error. How do we resolve this?
question_variants: Why does setting RF 1/1 = Supported cause a Consistency Check Invalid?
How do I register a Class 1 Bluetooth module without triggering ICS inconsistency?
What is the difference between RF Class 1 and RF PHY Class 1 in ICS?
actual_issue: SIG Check Rule: 'If RF(1/1) is Supported, then LMP(31/1) is Mandatory.' Setting RF ICS item 1/1 = Supported (Class 1 power output) requires LMP item 31/1 (LMP Power Control) to be Mandatory. If the included QDID's LL layer does not support LMP Power Control (31/1), the Consistency Check produces an Invalid error that cannot be cleared. The solution: set RF 1/1 = NO (Class 2 in RF layer) AND set RF PHY 1/15 = YES (PHY Class 1 = Class 1 power output at the RF PHY layer). This combination clears all Invalid errors while still accurately representing Class 1 power output capability through the RF PHY layer. RF/RF PHY testing should be conducted at Class 1 settings (PHY Class 1).
plain_english_explanation: The Bluetooth ICS has two places where output power class can be expressed: the RF layer (item 1/1) and the RF PHY layer (item 1/15). Setting RF 1/1 = Supported (Class 1) triggers a mandatory dependency on LMP Power Control (31/1). If the underlying QDID does not support that LMP item, you get an Invalid error. The workaround is to express Class 1 capability through the RF PHY layer instead: set RF 1/1 = NO (which relaxes the LMP dependency) and set RF PHY 1/15 = YES (PHY Class 1). This correctly expresses that the module is capable of Class 1 power output via the RF PHY item, without triggering the problematic LMP 31/1 dependency. Actual RF testing should still be done at Class 1 power levels to match the RF PHY ICS setting.
consultant_answer: Do not set RF 1/1 = Supported (this triggers LMP 31/1 Mandatory dependency). Instead: set RF 1/1 = NO (Class 2 in RF layer) AND RF PHY 1/15 = YES (PHY Class 1). This clears all Invalid errors while correctly representing Class 1 output through the RF PHY layer. RF/RF PHY test should be conducted at Class 1 (PHY Class 1) settings.
decision_logic:
1. Check Rule: RF(1/1) Supported → LMP(31/1) Mandatory.
2. If included QDID does not support LMP 31/1 → Invalid when RF 1/1 = Supported.
3. Solution: RF 1/1 = NO + RF PHY 1/15 = YES.
4. RF PHY 1/15 = YES correctly represents Class 1 power output at the PHY layer.
5. No LMP 31/1 dependency is triggered by RF PHY 1/15.
6. RF/RF PHY test at Class 1 (PHY Class 1) settings.
final_recommendation: For any Class 1 module registration: never set RF 1/1 = Supported unless the QDID explicitly supports LMP 31/1. Use RF 1/1 = NO + RF PHY 1/15 = YES as the standard approach for Class 1 power representation. Confirm this combination with the customer's test plan before testing begins.
risk_if_done_wrong: Setting RF 1/1 = Supported when LMP 31/1 is not in the QDID creates an unresolvable Invalid error that blocks registration entirely. Setting RF 1/1 = NO without setting RF PHY 1/15 = YES fails to represent Class 1 capability at all, which is an inaccurate registration.
